gaps.sentence: Remember ___ your passport to the airport.
gaps.explanation: remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do something.

gaps.sentence: She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: He went on ___ even after the audience had left.
gaps.explanation: go on + -ing = continue the same activity; go on to do = do something next.

gaps.sentence: It's not worth ___ about the delay — nothing will change.
The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: My parents wouldn't let me ___ out past midnight.
gaps.explanation: 'Let someone do' — 'let' takes the bare infinitive.

gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)

gaps.sentence: We can't risk ___ the deadline again.
